{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-co-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"798a9f46ef256fe2fcd6649d61108bc1cf96a97f683399cdb208a169af3a4a9e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-co-class-std:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"bdc8d5a61f622fc6c91da0be8478dfb02615c007374129c91888edf82eb1b746","source_liveness_sha256":"1b8565daf88dec5a1936ad41ec3e529347f3ec6b06db1d191293e01d45d7ee05"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Backing up, traffic signals and signs","heading":"C — Backing up, traffic signals and signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Backing up, traffic signals and signs

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Before you get in to back up, look behind the vehicle, because small children and small objects cannot be seen from the driver seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
To reverse, keep a foot on the brake while shifting, grip the top of the wheel, the 12 o'clock spot, with your left hand, rest your right arm on the passenger seat back and look over your shoulder out the rear window. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Mirrors do not show the space right behind the car, so a rear-view camera, if you have one, is used together with mirrors and an over-the-shoulder look, never instead of them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Back up slowly and smoothly, steering a little toward where the rear should go; when turning in reverse, glance quickly to the front and sides and keep looking back until fully stopped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Traffic is controlled by signals, signs and pavement markings, and also by police, highway workers and school crossing guards, whose directions you are required to follow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Signal lights are normally arranged with red at the top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom, though some places use a single red, yellow or green light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
If a traffic signal is dark or not working properly, handle the intersection as a four-way stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
At a steady red light, stop and wait for green; after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and traffic, a right turn on red is allowed unless a sign forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Turning left on red is legal only when both streets are one-way, going from one onto the other, after you stop and yield, and only if no sign prohibits it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow light warns that red is coming next, so stop unless you are already inside the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A01
On a steady green you may go straight or turn either way unless a sign bans the turn, but first yield to any vehicle or pedestrian already in the intersection or the crosswalk next to it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A01
A lit red arrow means stop, and you may not turn in the direction it points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A01
A green arrow, shown alone or with another light, lets you turn the way it points; if the arrow goes dark while the round green stays on, you may still turn after yielding to through traffic and pedestrians unless a sign or red arrow forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is about to appear, so stop unless you are already in the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow arrow lets a left-turning driver go carefully only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; it then turns solid yellow, meaning do not enter if you can stop safely, and finally red, meaning stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A01
Treat a flashing red light exactly like a stop sign: come to a stop, then move on once pedestrians and other traffic have been given the right of way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead, so slow down and continue with caution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A01
A HAWK signal, short for High Intensity Activated Crosswalk, helps pedestrians cross by flashing a yellow and red sequence that tells drivers someone needs to cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A01
Signs tell you rules, hazards, where you are, directions and nearby services, and a sign's shape and color show what kind of message it carries. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs state the law at a location, use black or red on a white background, and disobeying one is a traffic violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A01
Speed limit signs give the highest or lowest speed allowed; the highest limit assumes ideal conditions, so you must slow down when conditions demand it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A01
At a stop sign, stop completely at the marked stop line; with no line, stop before the near-side crosswalk; with neither, stop at the point closest to the cross road where you can see approaching traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A01
A yield sign means slow down, or stop if needed, to let every pedestrian and any vehicle that has the right of way go first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A02
Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs warn and turn back drivers heading the wrong way on a street or freeway ramp; never drive past one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A02
A One Way sign means you may travel only in the direction its arrow points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A02
Lane control signs, placed beside or above the road and often using arrows, show where you may turn; similar arrows are sometimes painted on the pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A02
Prohibited signs show an action you may not take, such as making a U-turn or a left turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A02
Warning signs are yellow or fluorescent green with black symbols and alert you to things like school zones, curves, slippery pavement, merging traffic or busy pedestrian areas; a merge sign, for example, warns of cars joining from a side street. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A02
Advisory speed signs are cautionary signs giving the safe speed for curves, corners and off-ramps under ideal conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A02
Railroad crossing signs come in several shapes; never race a train, never start across until there is room for your whole vehicle beyond the far side, and do not shift gears on the tracks in case the engine stalls. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A02
Blue railroad emergency notification system signs at every highway-rail grade crossing list a phone number for reporting problems, and the Department of Transportation number printed below it identifies that exact crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A02
Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols and are used with other devices or flaggers to steer traffic through work areas and protect road workers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A02
Guide signs have a green background and give directions and mileage to particular destinations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A02
Blue signs direct you to service facilities, while brown signs mark recreational, historic or cultural areas. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]
